title: Stereotaxic surgery for implantation of guide cannulas for microinjection into the dorsomedial hypothalamus in young rats
author: Poole, McGavin, et al.

steps.title: Perfuse and fix brains
steps.instruction: Perform transcardial perfusion on each rat, then immerse the extracted brain in 4 % paraformaldehyde prepared in phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) for 24 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Cryoprotect brains in sucrose
steps.instruction: Transfer the fixed brains to 30 % sucrose solution in PBS and incubate for 24 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Section hypothalamus block
steps.instruction: Place each brain in a rat brain matrix (suitable for 35–175 g brains). Starting 1 mm anterior to the optic chiasm, cut a 6 mm coronal section that contains the hypothalamus using razor blades, then mount the section with the posterior side facing down on a freezing block pre‑cooled to –50 °C.

steps.title: Freeze block with embedding compound
steps.instruction: Coat the mounted brain section with Clear Frozen Section Compound, allow it to solidify, and keep it frozen at –50 °C.

steps.title: Cut and store cryosections
steps.instruction: Using a cryostat, cut the frozen block into 30 µm thick slices. Transfer each slice into a well of a 24‑well plate containing 0.02 % sodium azide in PBS and store the plates at 4 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Assess cannula placement histologically
steps.instruction: Examine the brain slices in a petri dish filled with PBS under a stereomicroscope to locate clear cannula tracks. Using an adult rat brain atlas, plot the cannula tip positions from representative slices. Consider a cannula correctly placed in the dorsomedial hypothalamus (DMH) if the tip is medial to the fornix, ventral to the mammillothalamic tract, and lies between 2.6 mm and 3.8 mm posterior to bregma. Exclude any animal whose cannula tip falls outside these boundaries from subsequent behavioral analyses.

substeps.instruction: View slices in PBS under a stereomicroscope to identify cannula tracks.
Reference the adult rat brain atlas and plot tip coordinates.
Check that tip is medial to fornix, ventral to mammillothalamic tract, and 2.6–3.8 mm posterior to bregma.
If criteria are not met, discard the animal’s data.
